BPF, BPS, and BPA were highly removed in WWTPs in China, while BPAF, and BPE were relatively resistant to removal.
five bisphenol analogs (BPs) were widely detected, with BPA being the most abundant one, in wastewater and sludge from seven wastewater treatment plants (WTPs) in Xiamen.
BPA, the most widely studied BPs, is still the most abundant BPs detected in wastewater and sludge, and BPS and BPF are the most abundant BPA replacement chemicals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the occurrence, fate, and mass balance of BPs in the WWTPs of Xiamen, providing a basis for risk assessment and control of BPs in WWTPs.
the occurrence and fate BPs in WWTPs, providing valuable data for the management of BPs in WWTPs.
the occurrence, removal and fate of BPA and its analogues in WWTPs in a Chinese city, providing useful information for the risk assessment of BPs in WWTPs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
WWTPs were effective for removing BPs from aqueous phase.
the removal of BPA and its analogues is not efficient in the WWTPs.

WWTPs are effective to remove most of BPs from the aqueous phase, while BPAF, which has the similar structure to BPA and BPF, was resistant to biotransformation and adsorption, and thus it was the most persistent BPs in WWTPs in this study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BPA, which has been banned, was still widely detected, while BPF and BPS were the dominant BPs in the wastewater and sludges.
BPs have a wide range of occurrence in wastewater and sludge in Xiamen city.
BPs were widely detected in the WWTPs of Xiamen City and the BPs removal efficiency was highly variable among the WWTPs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BPF and BPS are highly removed in WWTPs, while BPAF, which is a potential replacement of BPA, is resistant to WWTPs.
